title: Increased Volume Overhead Stowage Compartment with Revised Latch and Load Placard

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Deeper overhead stowage compartment giving one additional standard bag per bin bay, with a revised latch and a re-placarded load limit, introduced after boarding time studies attributed gate delays to bag stowage.

sections.reason: Three operators measured boarding time on this type against comparable narrow-body fleets and found between ninety seconds and three minutes of additional time per turn, almost all of it spent finding stowage in the aft half of the cabin. The commercial case is straightforward at that scale. Separately, the latch on the delivered bin was the highest-reported cabin defect item, with a reported failure to stay closed in flight at a rate of about one per eight hundred flight hours across the fleet, which produces a cabin crew report every time.
sections.description: The bin shell is replaced by a deeper item that takes the standard bag on its side, giving one additional bag per bay across the cabin. The partition sub-assembly D2520121808497 and the partition assembly D2520129009055 are replaced, the trim kit D2520122039443 is re-issued for the deeper aperture and the curtain rail D2520125397271 at the bay ends is moved 25 mm inboard. Floating nuts EN194394K6 and washers EN557515-96 are used at the new tie-rod positions. The latch is changed to a two-stage item that has to be lifted before it releases. Functional item 47DL, the bin light assembly, moves with the shell. The load placard changes from 68 kg to 79 kg per bay and every bay is re-placarded. Work is along the whole cabin in zones 241, 244 and 251.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 42 kg for the full cabin, distributed along the length, with a longitudinal centre of gravity effect of 0.05 per cent mean aerodynamic chord. No electrical load change beyond the relocated bin lighting. The bin is not interchangeable with the delivered item because the tie-rod positions change, and a mixed cabin is permitted only if the placard for each bay matches the bin fitted, which is stated explicitly. The emergency evacuation substantiation is re-run for the reduced head clearance at the aisle edge and is unchanged. Cabin crew procedures for securing the cabin are re-issued because the latch action is different.
sections.embodiment_note: Production cut-in at MSN C00612 in May 2023. Retrofit is by Service Bulletin CRN-25-2006 for the bin shells and CRN-25-2011 for the placard and latch work on aircraft that keep the delivered shell. A full cabin retrofit is four shifts with the cabin out of service, and most operators have taken it during a cabin refresh rather than on its own.

type_data.balance_impact: Distributed along the cabin, longitudinal CG shift 0.05 % MAC
type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN C00612, bin supply from two sources to protect the ramp
